claims.text: Language models demonstrate quantitative improvement with increasing scale.
Language models demonstrate new qualitative capabilities with increasing scale.
Model performance is poor in absolute terms compared with human expert rater performance.
Model calibration is poor in absolute terms compared with human expert rater performance.
Performance is remarkably similar across model classes including dense and sparse transformers.
Sparse transformers provide performance benefits over dense architectures.
Tasks involving a large knowledge or memorization component commonly improve gradually and predictably with scale.
Tasks exhibiting breakthrough behavior at a critical scale often involve multiple steps or components.
Tasks exhibiting breakthrough behavior at a critical scale often involve brittle metrics.
Social bias typically increases with scale in settings with ambiguous context.
Social bias increases associated with scale can be improved with prompting.

evidence.description: Language models demonstrate both quantitative improvement and new qualitative capabilities with increasing scale.
Findings include: model performance and calibration both improve with scale
but are poor in absolute terms (and when compared with rater performance)
performance is remarkably similar across model classes, though with benefits from sparsity
tasks that improve gradually and predictably commonly involve a large knowledge or memorization component
whereas tasks that exhibit 'breakthrough' behavior at a critical scale often involve multiple steps or components, or brittle metrics
social bias typically increases with scale in settings with ambiguous context, but this can be improved with prompting.

methodologies.name: Beyond the Imitation Game benchmark (BIG-bench)
methodologies.description: A collaborative benchmark consisting of 204 tasks across diverse topics designed to evaluate capabilities beyond current language models.

methodologies.name: Model Scaling Evaluation
methodologies.description: Evaluation of various transformer architectures across model sizes spanning millions to hundreds of billions of parameters.

methodologies.name: Human Expert Baselining
methodologies.description: A team of human expert raters performed all tasks in the benchmark to provide a strong performance baseline.

limitations.text: New qualitative capabilities of language models are as yet poorly characterized.
Model performance and calibration are poor in absolute terms compared to human experts.
Social bias typically increases with scale in settings with ambiguous context.

future_work.text: Inform future research and prepare for disruptive new model capabilities.
Ameliorate socially harmful effects of language models.
